messages:
anya: Quick follow-up from the reservoir autoscale sync earlier — I'm trying to nail down who owns what between the orchestration layer and the autoscaler for GPU reservoirs. TL;DR: we need clear boundaries so teams can reason about headroom, prewarm credits, and eviction safety without coupling both codepaths.

mike: +1. do you mean splitting policy (who decides when to scale) vs execution (how to actually bring nodes up)?

anya: Exactly. My proposal: orchestration (=operator/controller) owns node lifecycle and placement. Autoscaler owns intent: target reservoir size, credit accounting, and when to request extra headroom. The operator implements the request to create capacity and enforces safety guards.

julia: That seems reasonable. One edge: eviction decisions need both signals (cost/packing from operator, SLO from autoscaler). who arbitrates conflicts?

anya: Good point. My thinking — autoscaler exposes an "eviction-preference" score per tenant. Operator can override only for cluster stability (emergency drains, fragmentation), otherwise obey preference.

sam: Implementation nit: how do we transport intent? CRD vs annotating existing resources? I prefer a small CRD with versioned spec so we can evolve.

anya: Agree on CRD. Sketch: ReservoirIntent CRD with fields: desired_size, headroom_pct, prewarm_budget, eviction_hint. It would be read by operator and controller.

mike: We should keep a guardrail: operator must reject intents that would blow commit budgets or violate tenancy quotas. Also need a fast fail path when node creation fails repeatedly -> exponential backoff.

julia: Observability reqs: we need tokenized metrics back to the autoscaler and product teams. token_count, pending_prewarm, actual_headroom, recent_evictions. Without those it's hard to tune headroom_pct.

anya: Agreed — add metrics contract in the doc. Minimal set: reservoir_desired_size, reservoir_actual_size, headroom_pct_target, headroom_bytes_available, eviction_score_sum.

ops-bot: NOTE: past incidents show a subtle race where two autoscalers requested headroom and operator interleaved placement -> double-counted. Need idempotency via intent version and admission controller. :warning:

derek: +1 on admission controller. also add a simple lease token model so autoscaler can claim an intent for N seconds to avoid dupes.

sam: quick config example I sketched (for discussion):
```yaml
apiVersion: infra.redwood.ai/v1
kind: ReservoirIntent
spec:
  desiredSize: 12
  headroomPct: 0.12
  prewarmBudget: 25 # tokens/sec
  evictionHint: "prefer-shrink-tenant=team-a"
  leaseTTLSeconds: 90
```

mike: nice. one more tradeoff: centralized autoscaler vs per-cluster. centralized simplifies global economics (cost bands) but adds latency for region-local spikes. maybe hybrid: per-region autoscalers with a global arbiter for cross-region cost caps.

anya: I like hybrid. we'll draft the operator API so either a local or a central autoscaler can write intents. include ownerRef field and origin.

julia: testing plan: sim harness that can play synthetic traffic and assert headroom <-> tail latency envelope. Also chaos test operator restarts during rollout.

anya: Action items: 1) I'll update the RFC with CRD sketch + metrics contract. 2) mike + derek to propose admission controller semantics. 3) sam to prototype leak-free lease model. 4) julia to list minimal dashboards and alerts.

mike: I'll open a PR for admission controller today, will ping the thread.

anya: Thanks all. If no objections I'll mark RFC follow-up and start the draft PRs. :rocket:

ops-bot: deploy-bot: linked docs: https://go.redwood.ai/rfc/reservoir-autoscale-draft (for reference)
